Dear Patient,

We are writing to update you about our masking guidance at Mass General Brigham clinics and hospitals. We have been monitoring respiratory virus activity in our community since the fall. Respiratory viruses in our community have been decreasing for several weeks. As of February 10, 2026 we have returned to a 
https://click.email.patientgateway.org/?%3D%3D 
mild/moderate level of activity.

At this activity level, Mass General Brigham employees are no longer required to wear masks during direct interactions with patients. Direct interactions with patients are in patient rooms or other clinical care areas where care is provided.

As a reminder, regardless of the time of year, please contact your care team if you have any of the following below before an in-person appointment:

	- Have a fever or other flu-like 
https://click.email.patientgateway.org/?%3D%3D 
symptoms .
	- Have an infection with a respiratory virus in the past 10 days.
Your care team will advise you about next steps. If you have an appointment in-person and meet any of the criteria above, you still need to wear one of our masks. 

Patients can always choose to wear a home respirator or mask to in-person appointments if they would like. 
https://click.email.patientgateway.org/?%3D%3D 
If you choose to wear your own respirator or mask , you must wear a facility-issued face mask on top of your own respirator or face mask. 

Thank you for taking the time to read this email.

Sincerely,

Tom Sequist, MD
Chief Medical Officer
Mass General Brigham

<p><a rel=3Dnofollow style=3D"text-decoration:none; color:#455A64">Hello Am=
ina</a>,</p>

<p><em>You may have previously received a notification regarding this updat=
e. If so, please disregard this message.</em></p>

<p>We=E2=80=99re writing to let you know that <strong>Cloud Observability</=
strong> has launched a new <a href=3Dhttps://c.gle/AEJ26qukbGVOP5bo7uVnfAtI=
76_z1ddJ887Ia5wRF46vxBzSiqswNzAdABLp4TR3Ajdh74vR0pizbse8tYHLwbHFNzVBYEgGIWx=
8nzH1Z35J2Cm-gfzl6eRQVSsfJQTjKd3x_XFW6pJ-oOeZ0WwuctOdLdJChuoVUDomCT316fWWuJ=
2RX5Gyk6KlMfY style=3D"color:#1a73e8; font-family:Roboto, arial; font-size:=
14px; text-decoration:none" target=3D_blank><strong>OpenTelemetry (OTel)</s=
trong> ingestion API</a> that supports native <strong>OpenTelemetry Protoco=
l (OTLP)</strong> logs, trace spans, and metrics.</p>

<p>Starting <strong>March 23, 2026</strong>, this API will be added as a de=
pendency for the current <strong>Cloud Logging</strong>, <strong>Cloud Trac=
e</strong>, and <strong>Cloud Monitoring</strong> ingestion APIs. This chan=
ge ensures a seamless transition as collection tools migrate to this new un=
ified endpoint.</p>

<h3>What you need to know</h3>

<p><strong>Key changes:</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>The existing Cloud Observability ingestion APIs (<a rel=3Dnofollow><c=
ode style=3Dcolor:#898989>logging.googleapis.com</code></a>, <a rel=3Dnofol=
low><code rel=3Dnofollow style=3Dcolor:#898989>cloudtrace.googleapis.com</c=
ode></a>, and <a rel=3Dnofollow><code rel=3Dnofollow style=3Dcolor:#898989>=
monitoring.googleapis.com</code></a>) are automatically activated when you =
create a Google Cloud project using the <strong>Google Cloud console</stron=
g> or <a rel=3Dnofollow><code style=3Dcolor:#898989>gcloud</code></a> CLI. =
The behavior remains unchanged for projects created via API, which do not h=
ave these ingestion APIs enabled by default. Starting <strong>March 23, 202=
6</strong>, the new OTel ingestion endpoint <a rel=3Dnofollow><code style=
=3Dcolor:#898989>telemetry.googleapis.com</code></a> will automatically act=
ivate when any of these specified APIs are enabled.</li>
  <li>In addition, we will automatically enable this new endpoint for all e=
xisting projects that already have current ingestion APIs active.</li>
</ul>

<h3>What you need to do</h3>

<p>No action is required from you for this API enablement change, and there=
 will be no disruption to your existing services. You may disable the API a=
t any time by following these <a href=3Dhttps://c.gle/AEJ26qv44aeDZcGbrPBsZ=
wpzEW89hxol7raGtV7dFkiiHYQlb-G4Uze12K4ioh7SQ6KRpYjsYURHlTeCVYQ3tu7_ayEzo7GU=
-D3jdmPMFqMMLVUPJoAhc-a4tPCYazYaN4auzTr5Uu_wze-c96DwBfIsuNUuKNDTCZNXGqQ_cVI=
 style=3D"color:#1a73e8; font-family:Roboto, arial; font-size:14px; text-de=
coration:none" target=3D_blank>instructions</a>.</p>

<p>Refer to the attachment for a list of the projects that will automatical=
ly enable the new endpoint.</p>

<h3>We=E2=80=99re here to help</h3>

<p>If you have any questions or require assistance, please contact <a href=
=3Dhttps://c.gle/AEJ26qsAsG8SqMGKRMJeqMHB_O2B0xY7HRohtC3WUayPMKyaMXN-lsQqOK=
TcZuZmQah0iolRt9KDUSGqeOwWpv3eb3eZBu6piIlQ4c2R1oOYZ1BTirv3rGMWwsk style=3D"=
color:#1a73e8; font-family:Roboto, arial; font-size:14px; text-decoration:n=
one" target=3D_blank>Google Cloud Support</a>.</p>

<p>Thanks for choosing Google Cloud Observability.</p>

she said. "I felt like I still built a relationship with the instructors ev=
en with them being far away."
